data.name: Jitendra
data.gender_notes: Jitendra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Jitendra is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘jita’ meaning victory and ‘indra’ meaning inner self or mind. This name signifies the victory of the inner self over external challenges. In Hindu mythology, Jitendra is the name of a deity who is believed to bestow inner strength and courage. The name Jitendra carries the meaning “Victory of the inner self” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jitendra usually hope their child will grow to embody victory of the inner self and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Jitendra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory of the inner self.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jitendra total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jitendra carries a rich cultural significance in Hindu tradition. It is a strong and evocative moniker that represents the triumph of the spirit over adversity. This name is often given to children as a source of inspiration, reminding them of their inner power and the potential for greatness within them. The name Jitendra is synonymous with valiance and is revered in many Indian communities as a symbol of strength and resilience.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Jitendra is multifold. It is a reminder of the victory of the soul over the challenges and hardships of the external world. The name embodies the concept of inner strength and serves as a constant reminder to seek inner peace and wisdom. In Hindu mythology, Jitendra is equated with the gods Indra and Vishnu, both of whom are revered for their power and ability to conquer obstacles. The name Jitendra is therefore an invocation of the divine power within oneself, inspiring one to rise above the mundane trials of life and seek spiritual growth and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jitendra: Conqueror of the Indras (Gods). One who has mastered their inner Indra, symbolizing inner strength, courage, and victory over inner struggles.

vedic_reference.note: Jitendra is a name of Indra, the god of rain and thunder in Hinduism.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Jitendra was a famous Maratha king who ruled the kingdom of Maratha from 1696 to 1707 AD. The name Jitendra carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
Jitendra Shahi was a Rajput king of the Chandradhagi branch of the Chandela dynasty, who ruled the Harijan kingdom from 1270 to 1310 AD.
